newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index hits record at opening.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index hits record at opening.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chip Hang Seng Index rallied to a record high at the opening on Thursday, jumping 161 points to 16,144 led by a strong advance in the property sector.
The index later extended its gains to hit an all-time high of 16,243.65. Turnover was HK$4.46 billion after the first half hour of trade.
"Developers' stocks have become the leaders of the market again. A lot of people think this is a new rally," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP-PrimeEast Securities.

"During the first half of the year, most of the stocks that went up were the laggard stocks like utilities while the conglomerates and developers were in consolidation. Recently we have seen renewed interest in them."
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd surged HK$3.25 to HK$84.00 and Swire Pacific Ltd gained HK$1.25 to HK$70.75.
Analysts said they were encouraged by the companies' recent property sales.

Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities, said the Hang Seng Index's rise above 16,000 points had persuaded investors that stocks were heading higher. The index broke through that level for the first time on Wednesday.
"It was psychological resistance. Now the market has broken through, people think it is going higher," said Galbraith.

China Resources Enterprise Ltd and Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd joined the Hang Seng Index on Thursday. China Resources rose HK$0.70 to HK$38.70 and Cheung Kong Infrastructure fell HK$0.10 to HK$26.80.
China Southern Airlines Co Ltd made its market debut, opening at HK$5.00 compared with an issue price of HK$4.70. The stock later came off its high to trade at HK$4.85.
CCT Telecom Holdings Ltd soared HK$0.29 to HK$1.64 after announcing that it would set up joint venture companies in China with a company controlled by China's Ministry of Electronics Industry.
